input: Deep clean the oven and stovetop burners

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing exactly which parts are included (oven interior, racks, door glass, burner grates, drip pans, knobs) determines how many steps and how much time the plan needs.
The type of oven (self-cleaning, conventional, gas vs. electric stovetop) completely changes which methods and products are safe and appropriate.
How much time is available affects whether a long soak or the self-clean cycle can be used, or whether a quick-turnaround method is needed.
Whether the user prefers natural/DIY cleaners (baking soda, vinegar) vs. commercial degreasers changes the product list and safety precautions entirely.
Knowing what cleaning supplies and tools are already on hand avoids recommending products that need to be purchased first.
If others (children, pets, people with sensitivities) are in the home during cleaning, it affects ventilation needs and which chemical cleaners are safe to use.
Understanding what level of cleanliness counts as 'done' — sparkling showroom finish vs. functionally clean and grease-free — calibrates how intensive the plan should be.

gold.taskTitle: Deep clean oven and stovetop burners
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to thoroughly clean their oven interior and stovetop burners, going beyond routine wiping to remove grease, grime, and baked-on residue.

questions.title: Which oven and stovetop parts need cleaning?
questions.description: Should the plan cover only the oven interior and burners, or also oven racks, door glass, drip pans, burner grates, and knobs?

questions.title: What type of oven and stovetop do you have?
questions.description: Is it a gas or electric stovetop, and is the oven a standard/conventional model or does it have a self-cleaning function?

questions.title: How much time can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Do you have a few hours today, or do you need this done in under an hour? This determines whether overnight soaking or a self-clean cycle is viable.

questions.title: Do you prefer natural cleaners or commercial products?
questions.description: Would you rather use DIY solutions like baking soda and vinegar, or are store-bought degreasers and oven cleaners like Easy-Off acceptable?

questions.title: What cleaning supplies do you already have at home?
questions.description: Knowing what tools and products are on hand — scrub brushes, microfiber cloths, degreaser, baking soda — avoids a plan that requires a shopping trip first.

questions.title: Will people or pets be home during the cleaning?
questions.description: The presence of children, pets, or anyone with respiratory sensitivities affects which cleaners are safe to use and how much ventilation is required.

questions.title: What does a successful clean look like to you?
questions.description: Are you aiming for a like-new, spotless finish, or is the goal simply removing heavy grease and burnt-on buildup so the oven functions cleanly?
